title: fix(record-context): a related object's read that fails is a failure, not a refusal
body:
Fixes #37463

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：AI 用资料包读一条记录时，如果关联对象那一步因为故障（比如数据库抖动）读不出来，现在回答「服务暂时不可用」，不再谎称「无权访问」；对有权限的拒绝照旧。用户无感于正常路径。
- 为什么做：属于「记录级 AI 问答」专题，替核对 AI 回答引用的一方解决分不清「没权限」和「出故障」的问题，故障时引用会被如实上报而不是悄悄丢掉。
- 出错会怎样：最坏情况是某次故障被报成「暂时不可用」，调用方重试即可；回答里不会多说出任何对象、字段或包的名字，改动可直接撤回。
- 要你做的：无。

## What changes

`get_record_context` (`packages/services/service-record-context`) reads each related object of a pack before it answers. At four of those reads, a throw that was **not** a refusal (an outage, a bug) was answered as `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, so the citation verifier (`verifyRecordCitations`) read it as a refusal and dropped every citation without a report:

| Site | Before (uncoded throw) | After |
|---|---|---|
| step 4a, `assertApiExposed` failure that is not an API-exposure refusal | 403 unnamed | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| step 4a, `servedObjectDefinitionOf(child)` throwing | 403 unnamed | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| `publishedOf`, published-definition read throwing | 403 unnamed | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| the child list query throwing | the raw error rethrown | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |

- **One classifier, two readers.** `isCodedRefusal` (in `record-context-tools.ts`, not on the package entry) is the ADR-0112 line: a non-empty string `code` plus a declared 4xx status (`.status`, then `.statusCode`). The executor asks it at all four sites through one helper (`refusedOrFailed`); the verifier now imports the same function in place of its private copy, so the two can not drift.
- **A coded refusal answers as before.** At the three object-level sites it stays `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 within the naming bound; a disabled package's `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` (404, coded) is such a refusal. At the child list query the door's own coded refusal is rethrown as the door wrote it, exactly as on `main` (the child already passed step 4a, so it is served to the caller).
- **A failure names nothing.** Its sentence (`sentences.ts` `readFailed`, en and zh-Hans) names the pack and the root only. The original error rides on `cause` for the host (the verifier hands it to `onError`). Measured: `mapDataError` (the `/data` classifier both MCP doors answer with) answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with the error text `Internal server error` whatever `cause` holds — tried with no cause, a plain error, a SQLite and a Postgres unique violation, `SQLITE_BUSY`, and a coded 403.
- `verify-citations.ts`: the docblock paragraph that said the executor turns these failures into a 403 was made false by this change and is rewritten.

### ADR-0160 (card item 3)

No ADR-0160 sentence fixes 403 for a failed read. The two sentences closest are about refusals only:

> Every such refusal carries one code — `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the code #35145 uses — so the code does not tell a hidden object from a refused one. (D4, "The naming bound")

> An object-level refusal names the refused object only when the caller's served schema shows it, and every such refusal carries one code. (point 12)

D3 "Object level" covers refusals by gates and says nothing on reads that fail. So no ADR text has to change for this PR; whether to add a sentence on failures stays with #37490.

## Tests

- `record-context-tools.test.ts`, new `describe` "a read of a related object that fails is a failure, not a refusal": one uncoded-throw case per site (503, the exact `readFailed` sentence, none of the outage's names, the original on `cause`); a refusal control per object-level site (`OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` 404 stays `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, unnamed) and for the child query (the door's coded refusal is rethrown unchanged); a driver errno with no status, a coded 5xx, a status with no code, and a thrown string are failures too; the sentence follows the caller's locale. The old case pinning an uncoded served-definition throw as 403 now pins a coded refusal there instead.
- `verify-citations.test.ts`: an uncoded throw at the child's served-definition read drops the citation and is reported once through `onError` (503, cause is the outage); a coded refusal there drops it and reports nothing; a control that verifies the same citation.
- `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts`, the real-kernel harness: the related list read of `rc_revision` throws an uncoded error in `engine.find`; both doors answer the same bytes, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503, with no object name and no outage text in them; the control call reads once the spy is removed.

## Acceptance notes

- What a coded refusal from the child list query does is unchanged (it is rethrown, the door's own text). The card does not ask for that site's refusal path to change, so it is left as it is.
- The naming-probe read inside the step 4a exposure catch (`servedObjectDefinitionOf(...).catch(() => null)`) still treats a throw as "not shown". The refusal is a real one, so a throw there only leaves out the object's name.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `record-context-tools.ts` `refusedOrFailed` and the four `catch` sites that call it.
2. `record-context-tools.ts` `isCodedRefusal`, and `verify-citations.ts` now importing it.
3. `sentences.ts` `readFailed`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-record-context exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/__tests__/record-context-tools.test.ts` — expect the new `describe` to pass, all of it.
